title: Cost and Resource Optimization on Google Cloud
bodyMarkdown:
## Why this matters for the PCA exam

Cost optimization is a recurring exam theme that bridges technical and business processes. You need to know the **pricing levers**, the **tools** that find waste, and the **financial model** (CapEx vs OpEx) that frames the conversation with leadership.

## CapEx vs OpEx

- **CapEx (capital expenditure):** large upfront purchases of hardware/data centers, depreciated over years. Requires forecasting peak capacity and over-provisioning.
- **OpEx (operating expenditure):** pay-as-you-go consumption. Cloud shifts most spend to OpEx, improving cash flow and aligning cost with usage - but it demands active governance to avoid waste.

## Compute pricing levers (know the differences cold)

| Mechanism | Commitment | Discount | Best for |
|-----------|-----------|----------|----------|
| **On-demand** | None | None | Spiky, unpredictable, short-lived |
| **Sustained use discounts (SUDs)** | None (automatic) | Modest, applied automatically as a VM runs most of the month | Steady usage you have not committed |
| **Committed use discounts (CUDs)** | 1 or 3 years | Deep | Stable, predictable baseline |
| **Spot VMs** | None | Very deep | Fault-tolerant, interruptible batch |

### CUD flavors
- **Spend-based (flexible) CUDs:** commit to an hourly dollar amount of spend; apply across machine families and regions - maximum flexibility.
- **Resource-based CUDs:** commit to specific vCPU/memory in a region/family - good when the shape is fixed.

> Exam pattern: stable 24/7 baseline + no machine-type lock-in => **flexible (spend-based) CUDs**. Interruptible batch => **Spot**. Unpredictable short bursts => on-demand (SUDs apply automatically).

## Finding and removing waste

- **Active Assist / Recommender:** machine-type **rightsizing**, **idle VM / disk / IP** recommendations, idle GKE and Cloud SQL insights, and **CUD recommendations** based on real utilization.
- **Rightsizing:** match machine size to actual CPU/memory use; downsize over-provisioned VMs and nodes.
- **Scheduling:** stop non-production resources off-hours (instance schedules / automation) - dev/test idle time is pure waste.
- **Storage tiering:** move cold data to Nearline/Coldline/Archive; set Object Lifecycle Management rules.
- **Autoscaling:** scale compute (MIGs, GKE, Cloud Run) to demand instead of provisioning for peak.

## Visibility and governance

- **Cloud Billing reports & BigQuery billing export** for detailed, queryable spend analysis.
- **Billing budgets & alerts:** set percentage thresholds (e.g., 50/90/100%) on actual or forecasted spend; email billing admins; publish to **Pub/Sub** to automate responses. Budgets are **not** hard caps - any automatic shutoff is something you build.
- **Labels** on resources to allocate cost by team/environment/app (showback/chargeback).
- **FinOps culture:** make engineers cost-aware; review spend in regular business reviews.

## A practical optimization order

1. **Eliminate idle** (schedules, delete unused) - immediate, low risk.
2. **Rightsize** with Recommender - low risk.
3. **Tier storage** and tune autoscaling.
4. **Commit** (CUDs) only after usage is stable and understood.

## Key takeaways

- Cloud shifts **CapEx -> OpEx** but needs governance.
- Know **on-demand vs SUD vs CUD (flexible/resource) vs Spot** and when each wins.
- Use **Recommender** to rightsize and find idle resources; schedule off-hours shutdowns.
- Set **budgets with Pub/Sub** for alerting/automation; remember budgets are not hard caps.
